S-KUAC.outlet: KUAC, syndicated by Alaska Public Media
S-KUAC.author: Patrick Gilchrist
S-KUAC.note: KUAC original and the APM syndication are the SAME reporting and do not corroborate each other. Every Fairbanks claim is single-sourced.

S-MUNI.outlet: Municipality of Anchorage, Assembly member profiles

claims.label: roughly, per Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: roughly $600,000 worth of audio visual equipment that requires approval from the Anchorage Assembly
claims.note: SAY ROUGHLY. A separate listing put it near $599,000 inside a larger $1.4M appropriation.

claims.spoken: up to seven hundred fifty volunteered feeds
claims.label: capacity, per Alaska's News Source, September 2025
claims.verbatim: allow for up to 750 video feeds into APD from residents or businesses who volunteer to register
claims.note: HARD BLOCKER. 750 is a CEILING on volunteered private feeds, not a live camera count. No current count is published anywhere. A card reading '750 cameras watching Anchorage' would be FALSE.

claims.label: per Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: Any further action on the three-year contract with Thundercat Technology Inc. was postponed to the Anchorage Assembly meeting of August 18
claims.note: POSTPONED, not rejected and not blocked.

claims.spoken: the Assembly wrote a rule naming facial recognition
claims.label: Anchorage Municipal Code ch. 3.102, adopted April 2023
claims.verbatim: The ordinance doesn't ban the use of facial recognition technology indefinitely, however, if the city opts to purchase and use the technology, the Assembly must approve it, and there must be a public hearing
claims.note: NOT A BAN. Passed 10 to 1 on April 18th 2023. Heavily limits. Carve-outs for human remains, missing persons, trafficking and child-abuse cases. The film says 'wrote a rule naming facial recognition' and never says banned.

claims.label: per Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: The Assembly voted to bar the use of facial recognition in 2023, but Case said APD does use object recognition for their license plate readers

claims.spoken: the plate readers run object recognition
claims.label: Chief Sean Case, via Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: Case said APD does use object recognition for their license plate readers.
claims.note: SCOPE. Plate readers ONLY. Never widen to the volunteered feeds, the drones or the body cameras.

claims.spoken: Assembly member Keith McCormick says the code can't say what's collected, or who sees it
claims.on_screen: "THE CODE CAN'T ANSWER ANY OF THOSE QUESTIONS"
claims.label: Assembly Member Keith McCormick, District 6
claims.verbatim: when my constituents ask, 'what are we collecting? Who can see it? How long do we keep it?' Anchorage code can't answer any of those questions. We have no legislative guardrails.
claims.note: HIS CHARACTERIZATION, not a finding. Code ch. 3.102 titled Municipal Use of Surveillance Technologies DOES exist. Attribute on screen.

claims.spoken: He'd come to a committee first. Generally.
claims.on_screen: "WE WILL COME TO THE BODY GENERALLY"
claims.label: Police Chief Sean Case, via Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: And prior to using any of those sorts of pieces of technology, we will come to the body generally in the form of the Public Health and Safety Committee, so that the body is aware of what we're doing

claims.label: Police Chief Sean Case, via Alaska's News Source
claims.verbatim: It's our response to crime. We think it's going to have a significant impact, but we are not going to outrun our coverage on this, and that's the commitment that we made.
claims.note: COUNTER-POINT. Do NOT write 'significant impact on crime'. The words 'on crime' are not on the page.

claims.on_screen: "CUT DOWN ON US COMING IN TOO HOT"
claims.label: Chief Sean Case, Alaska Public Media, September 2025
claims.verbatim: It's going to cut down on us coming in too hot, because we just have better information.
claims.note: THE STRONGEST HONEST COUNTER-POINT for Anchorage. A de-escalation argument in the chief's own mouth.

claims.label: city camera footage, per Alaska's News Source, September 2025
claims.verbatim: all data will be stored for 14 days unless detectives store it as evidence. Then, it will be held for two years.
claims.note: Scoped to CITY cameras by APM. Whether the same clock governs volunteered private feeds is not stated anywhere.

claims.spoken: It put artificial intelligence on redacting body camera video
claims.label: Chief of Staff Mike Sanders, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: Sanders told the council that they'd enlisted artificial intelligence in hopes of speeding up the process, but that it's still too slow.
claims.note: THE SOURCE NEVER ITEMISES WHAT IS REDACTED. Do not put a list of redacted categories on screen. The film paints a redaction and labels it only REDACTED.

claims.label: neither KUAC nor Alaska Public Media names a vendor or product
claims.verbatim: (verified ABSENCE of any vendor or product name on either page)
claims.note: Stated on screen because it is load-bearing for the procurement question.

claims.on_screen: APRIL: MORE THAN 35 / JULY: MORE THAN 35
claims.label: Fairbanks city clerk data, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: Monthly data provided by the city clerk's office spanning May 2023 to July 2026 show requests for Fairbanks police audio and video peaked this year, surpassing 35 in both April and July.
claims.note: SURPASSING 35 means MORE THAN 35. A flat '35' understates it.

claims.label: Fairbanks city clerk data, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: Prior to October 2025, those kinds of requests hadn't exceeded 20 in any single month

claims.label: per KUAC
claims.verbatim: the time-consuming process of redacting the audio and video gets in the way of the police department's evidence technician performing other essential job duties

claims.spoken: basically subsidizing YouTubers from the Lower Forty-Eight
claims.on_screen: "BASICALLY JUST SUBSIDIZING YOUTUBERS FROM THE LOWER 48"
claims.label: Chief of Staff Mike Sanders, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: Instead, he's basically just subsidizing YouTubers from the Lower 48,
claims.note: The 'he' is THE EVIDENCE TECHNICIAN, singular. Misreading the pronoun would invert the sentence.

claims.spoken: free under five staff hours a month
claims.on_screen: FREE UNDER 5 STAFF HOURS A MONTH
claims.label: state law as described by Chief Ron Dupee, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: state law that makes receiving public records free as long as providing them doesn't require more than five hours of staff time in a calendar month
claims.note: akleg.gov returned 403 so the statute text was NOT independently confirmed. Attribute to the chief.

claims.label: Police Chief Ron Dupee, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: And number two, we just don't have the personnel to keep up with the requests. At the end of the day, that's the biggest issue,
claims.note: THE FAIRBANKS COUNTER-POINT in the city's own mouth. A staffing claim, not an anti-transparency claim.

claims.spoken: tell them you'll get it when you get it
claims.on_screen: "YOU'LL GET IT WHEN YOU GET IT"
claims.label: Chief of Staff Mike Sanders, via KUAC
claims.verbatim: By telling these YouTubers, like, "You'll get it when you get it,"
claims.note: MUST SHIP WITH c21. Without it the film implies this is city policy. It is not.

claims.spoken: Its own attorneys disagreed that night
claims.label: per KUAC
claims.verbatim: Sanders acknowledged that the city attorney's office doesn't agree with that method.
claims.note: MANDATORY companion to c20. The fact-check named omitting this as the single most unfair cut available in this story.

claims.label: Municipality of Anchorage
claims.verbatim: District 1 - North Anchorage: Sydney Scout, Daniel Volland. District 6 - South Anchorage, Girdwood, Turnagain Arm: Zac Johnson, Keith McCormick.
claims.note: Attribution check for c7. McCormick is District 6.

cut_list: 'The Assembly BANNED facial recognition' — it heavily limits, is not indefinite, and has carve-outs.
'750 cameras' as a live count — 750 is a ceiling on volunteered feeds.
'15-camera current footprint' — not published anywhere. DEAD.
'significant impact on crime' — the words 'on crime' are not on the page.
The Flock 'completely different' + 'come with the equipment' splice — two answers to two different questions.
Drones, body cameras and plate readers as part of the AUGUST 2026 request — they belong to the September 2025 contract.
A list of what the Fairbanks AI redacts — the source never itemises it.
Any Fairbanks AI vendor or product name — none published.
Any figure for hours Fairbanks staff actually spend — not published.
Rep. Ashley Carrick speaking — she is named as HB 377's sponsor and is not quoted.
Assembly Member Erin Baldwin-Day speaking — she asks a question and is not quoted.

John McKay's 'most harmful since statehood' — it attaches to HB 377, a bill this film does not cover. Splicing it onto the chief of staff's remark would manufacture a judgment nobody made. The whole HB 377 thread is cut.
'out of state' — the sources say Lower 48 and Outside.
illustrative_note: Every on-screen number is illustrative of the cited claim and is not a live feed. The pairing of the two cities is THIS FILM'S ARGUMENT and no source links them.
